Initialize spaCy

Source: R/spacy_initialize.R
spacy_initialize.Rd

Initialize spaCy to call from R.

Usage

spacy_initialize(
  model = "en_core_web_sm",
  entity = TRUE,
  max_length = NULL,
  split_hyphens = TRUE,
  entity_patterns = NULL,
  overwrite_entities = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

Language package for loading spaCy. Example: en_core_web_sm (English) and de_core_news_sm (German). Default is en_core_web_sm. This can also be the path to a model directory.

entity

logical; if FALSE is selected, named entity recognition is turned off in spaCy. This will speed up the parsing as it will exclude ner from the pipeline. For details of spaCy pipeline, see https://spacy.io/usage/processing-pipelines.

max_length

integer; the maximum number of characters in a single document that spaCy will accept (nlp.max_length), a whole number no larger than .Machine$integer.max. If NULL (the default), spaCy's default of 1,000,000 is used. Larger values require roughly 1GB of temporary memory per 100,000 characters for the parser and entity recogniser.

split_hyphens

logical; if TRUE (the default), words joined by a hyphen are split as the language model's tokenizer splits them, which for English makes three tokens of "eye-opening": "eye", "-" and "opening". If FALSE, the tokenizer no longer splits at a single hyphen between letters, or between a letter and a digit, so that "eye-opening" stays one token, and the rest of the pipeline, such as the tagger and lemmatizer, processes it as one. Note that the default differs from that of quanteda's quanteda::tokens(), whose split_hyphens = FALSE keeps hyphenated words together by default. See Details.

entity_patterns

rule-based entities to add to the pipeline: a spacyr_entity_patterns object, or anything that as_entity_patterns() accepts, such as a named character vector of phrases. spacyr adds spaCy's entity ruler, as spacyr_entity_ruler, at the end of the pipeline, after every component that sets entities; an entity ruler saved with the model stays as it is. If the model already has a component of that name, for instance because it was saved from a pipeline with rules added by spacyr, the new ruler is named spacyr_entity_ruler_2 (or the next free number). If NULL (the default), the pipeline is not changed.

overwrite_entities

logical; where an entity matched by entity_patterns overlaps one found by an earlier component, such as the model's named entity recognizer, the rule's entity is kept if TRUE (the default), and the earlier one if FALSE, so that the rules only add entities where none were found.

...

not used.

Details

With entity_patterns, the entities found by the rules are returned by spacy_parse() and spacy_extract_entity() like any others, also when entity = FALSE. Patterns that ask for an entity type (ENT_TYPE) or for tokens inside an entity (ENT_IOB) build on the entities of earlier components, such as the model's ner or a ruler saved with the model, so they give a warning when no earlier component sets entities, for instance with entity = FALSE. Phrases are tokenized with the pipeline's own tokenizer, and those marked case_insensitive match the lower case form of each token. A component that changes the tokens, such as spaCy's merge_entities, can stop phrases from matching when it comes before the ruler, which gives a warning.

With split_hyphens = FALSE, the tokenizer still splits wherever the model's tokenizer did other than at a single hyphen within a word: between numbers, so that "3-4" is still three tokens ("3", "-" and "4"), where quanteda's tokens(split_hyphens = FALSE) keeps it as one; at two or more hyphens, as in "a–b"; and at the start or end of a word. The models were trained on text with hyphenated words split, so their tags, lemmas and dependencies for a hyphenated word kept whole can differ from those for its parts. Only the language's default infix rules are changed: a model saved with infix rules of its own, or whose tokenizer is not spaCy's rule-based one, as for Chinese and Japanese, is left as it is. A warning is given if the tokenizer still splits some hyphenated words, between letters or between a letter and a digit, for whatever reason. Many languages, such as German, do not split them in the first place. Phrase patterns of a ruler saved with the model, such as an entity_ruler, were tokenized when the model was saved, so those containing hyphenated words may no longer match; changing the tokenizer gives a warning when an active component has phrase patterns. Those of entity_patterns are tokenized after the change.

Phrases are matched quickly, even many thousands of them, and so are patterns of a single token with a regular expression, such as dictionary values with a wildcard, which spacyr combines into one regular expression for each label. Other token patterns are checked one by one, and so are phrases marked case_insensitive when the patterns also include phrases that are not, which makes parsing slower when there are many of them.

Unless the environment variable TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM is already set, spacy_initialize() sets it to "false". Pipelines that use Hugging Face's tokenizers library, such as some built with spacy-transformers, otherwise print a warning about disabling parallelism, with versions of tokenizers before 0.22.2, again and again until R is restarted, once the R process is forked after the library has been used, for instance by parallel::mcparallel(); saving a file in RStudio has also been reported to trigger it. The setting controls the library's tokenizer threads; its effect on total runtime depends on the pipeline and the workload. It applies to the whole R process, Python included, and stays after spacy_finalize(); if initialization fails, the previous value is restored. A value set before calling spacy_initialize() is kept, even an empty one, which tokenizers reads as "false". Setting Sys.setenv(TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM = "true") turns off the library's safeguard against deadlocks: a forked process, such as a worker of parallel::mclapply(), or of n_process greater than 1 when the workers are started by fork, that uses tokenizers after the parent has used it can then hang. Leave the setting at "false" whenever that can happen.

See also

as_entity_patterns()

Author

Akitaka Matsuo, Johannes B. Gruber

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# academic titles as part of a person's name
titles <- c("dr", "dr.", "prof", "prof.", "professor")
pats <- as_entity_patterns(list(
    label = "PERSON",
    pattern = list(list(LOWER = list(IN = titles)),
                   list(ENT_TYPE = "PERSON", ENT_IOB = "B"),
                   list(ENT_TYPE = "PERSON", ENT_IOB = "I", OP = "*"))))
spacy_initialize(entity_patterns = pats)
spacy_extract_entity("Prof. Jane Smith met Dr Bob Jones in Paris.")
spacy_finalize()

# phrases, with labels as names
spacy_initialize(entity_patterns = c(ORG = "Acme Widgets", GPE = "Ruritania"))
spacy_finalize()
} # }
